mechanism_narrative: A significant week-on-week recovery in WORKPLACES mobility, following a sharp decline, indicates a return to office-based work and associated weekday activities, which will drive an increase in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES increases by more than 10 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, despite WORKPLACES increasing by more than 10 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decrease in residential mobility, falling below a key baseline threshold, suggests people are spending less time at home and more time out, directly translating to higher RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 6% from baseline and stays below for at least one week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days does not increase relative to the last 14 days, even when RESIDENTIAL falls below 6% from baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week decline in grocery and pharmacy mobility, even from high levels, signals a broader reduction in essential outings or consumer confidence, which will negatively impact non-essential RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls by more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days, despite GROCERY_PHARM falling by more than 5 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: The concurrent recovery in both transit station and workplace mobility indicates a broad return to daily commuting and out-of-home activities, creating more opportunities for retail and recreation, leading to higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both show week-on-week increases
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the last 28 days, despite both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES showing week-on-week increases.

mechanism_narrative: The persistent negative trend in RETAIL_REC mobility over the past four weeks, without strong counter-signals, indicates a baseline of reduced activity that will continue to keep RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is significantly higher than the average of the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: Consistently low parks mobility in mid-November suggests the onset of colder weather, reducing outdoor leisure activities and shifting consumer behavior away from associated retail, leading to lower RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility remains below -20% from baseline for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days increases, despite PARKS mobility remaining consistently below -20% from baseline.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of persistently above-baseline residential mobility and significantly below-baseline workplace mobility indicates a continued prevalence of remote work and home-based activities, which limits opportunities for out-of-home retail and recreation, leading to lower RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days, while RESIDENTIAL remains above 5% and WORKPLACES remains below -15% from baseline.

mechanism_narrative: High week-to-week volatility in transit station mobility reflects inconsistent travel patterns and general uncertainty in daily routines, which will hinder any sustained recovery in RETAIL_REC, keeping it lower over the next week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT week-on-week change exceeds 5 points in either direction for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days increases significantly, despite high week-on-week volatility in TRANSIT mobility.
